episodes.167587: A line of severe thunderstorms moved into the Berkshires late in the afternoon, out ahead of a cold front.  The storms weakened as they moved east but still caused isolated tree/wire damage in the slopes of the Berkshires and in Hartford County, CT.
episodes.167606: A cold front crossed central Pennsylvania during the late morning and early afternoon of May 16, 2022. Although the storms came through fairly early in the day, there was still enough instability and shear to enable a few of the storms to produce sporadic wind damage.
episodes.167607: An intense supercell thunderstorm spawned by a strong cold front and negatively-tilted upper-level trough resulted in a swatch of considerable wind damage and significant hail from parts of northern Virginia, across the southern suburbs of Washington DC, to southern Maryland.
episodes.167609: An intense supercell thunderstorm spawned by a strong cold front and negatively-tilted upper-level trough resulted in a swatch of considerable wind damage and significant hail from parts of northern Virginia, across the southern suburbs of Washington DC, to southern Maryland.
episodes.167610: Thunderstorms produced gale to storm force wind gusts and hail over the tidal Potomac River and middle portion of the Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.167620: A potent shortwave (mid-level disturbance) and a cold front moved into a marginal/moderate unstable airmass across northern NY during the afternoon of May 16th. Numerous showers and some scattered thunderstorms developed with a few storms producing severe weather in terms of localized damaging winds and/or hail of one inch in diameter.
episodes.167621: A potent shortwave (mid-level disturbance) and a cold front moved into a marginal/moderate unstable airmass across VT during the afternoon/evening hours of May 16th. Numerous showers and some scattered thunderstorms developed with a few storms producing severe weather in terms of localized damaging winds and/or hail of one inch in diameter.
episodes.167725: A strong cold front moved through the mid-Atlantic late on May 16. Multiple areas of convection developed ahead of the front. With moderate to strong instability and shear, the environment ahead of the front appeared favorable for widespread severe weather. However, a messy convective evolution served to limit the overall threat. The greatest frontal forcing also ultimately tracked further north. However, some storms still became strong to severe and produced a few instances of damaging winds and hail.
episodes.167726: A strong cold front moved through the mid-Atlantic late on May 16. Multiple areas of convection developed ahead of the front. With moderate to strong instability and shear, the environment ahead of the front appeared favorable for widespread severe weather. However, a messy convective evolution served to limit the overall threat. The greatest frontal forcing also ultimately tracked further north. However, some storms still became strong to severe and produced a few instances of damaging winds and hail.
episodes.167727: A strong cold front moved through the mid-Atlantic late on May 16. Multiple areas of convection developed ahead of the front. With moderate to strong instability and shear, the environment ahead of the front appeared favorable for widespread severe weather. However, a messy convective evolution served to limit the overall threat. The greatest frontal forcing also ultimately tracked further north. However, some storms still became strong to severe and produced a few instances of damaging winds and hail.
episodes.167805: A cold front passed through the region on May 16, 2022. This triggered several rounds of thunderstorms in the Proctor, VT area, producing between 2 and 3 inches of rainfall. Prior rainfall of a similar magnitude affected this same area two days prior (May 14), leading to saturated soils, and a susceptibility for flash flooding on the 16th.
episodes.168045: A cold front moved through Central New York, triggering multiple thunderstorms. An unstable environment supported many severe thunderstorms. While damaging wind gusts were the main hazard, large hail was also reported. Most of the damage was from trees and wires being knocked down. However, there was a surveyed microburst in Cayuga County near Venice Center that resulted in multiple farm buildings that had parts or all of their roof ripped off, a small farm building being knocked off its foundation by a large tree, and multiple large trees in the area snapped or knocked over.
episodes.168053: A cold front moved through Northeastern Pennsylvania, triggering a broken line of thunderstorms. An unstable environment allowed a few storms to become severe with damaging wind gusts as the main hazard.
episodes.168563: A strong cold front triggered scattered thunderstorms across the Mid-Atlantic region . One of these storms became severe, producing localized wind damage in Henry County.
episodes.168564: A strong cold front crossing the Mid-Atlantic region sparked scattered thunderstorms. A few of these storms produced damaging winds in Rockingham County.
episodes.168669: Cumulus congestus cloud lines enhanced by cyclonic and divergent upper tropospheric flow aloft resulted in numerous waterspouts.  Waterspouts initially developed near the upper Florida Keys, but eventually evolved near the more robust cloud line near the lower Florida Keys.
episodes.168714: Northeast Ohio resided in the warm sector during the afternoon and early evening of the 16th, when a pre-frontal surface trough moved east-southeastward through the area. Low-level convergence and associated ascent along the trough axis acted as a focus for the development of isolated showers and thunderstorms. One storm managed to produce penny-size hail. This convection occurred in an environment with weak to moderate MUCAPE and moderate effective bulk shear.
episodes.168716: Lake Erie resided in the warm sector during the afternoon and early evening of the 16th, when a pre-frontal surface trough moved east-southeastward across the lake. Low-level convergence and associated ascent along the trough axis acted as a focus for the development of isolated to scattered showers and thunderstorms. Some of this convection generated gale-force peak wind gusts along the lakeshore in northeast OH and northwest PA. The convection occurred in an environment with weak MUCAPE and moderate effective bulk shear.
episodes.168760: An upper level ridge was over West Texas. An upper level disturbance moved over the area which provided lift. A weak cold front had moved into the Permian Basin during the morning hours. These conditions resulted in a thunderstorm that produced a strong wind gust across the northwest Permian Basin.
episodes.168788: Thunderstorms developing over Goshen County during the afternoon of the 16th created strong outflow winds near Torrington with a measured wind gust of 64 mph.
episodes.168915: A broad low level trough extended from the Carolinas to northern Florida with PWAT between 1.2 and 1.4 inches across the local area. A mid to upper level trough was noted across GA to eastern Gulf of Mexico. Steeper mid level lapse rates were near 6.9 degC/km at JAX with unstable surface CAPE around 2600 J/kg today in the afternoon. Storms formed along the inland progressing sea breezes.
episodes.168997: A complex of severe thunderstorms shifted southeast out of Oklahoma and into portions of North and East Texas during the evening hours of May 15th, ahead of a weak cold front and associated shortwave trough that dove southeast through the Southern Plains. Ample shear and strong instability characteristic with steep lapse rates maintained the intensity of these storms as they entered Northeast Texas during the late evening, resulting in multiple reports of damaging winds over Franklin and Upshur Counties before the storms became more outflow dominant and quickly weakened as they shifted farther east into a more unfavorable environment.
episodes.169511: A cold front pushed across western New York triggering scattered thunderstorms over the northern Finger Lakes late in the morning. As these thunderstorms increased, a prolific amount of lightning occurred. The line then swept east across the North Country to the east of Lake Ontario into the afternoon producing straight line wind damage.
episodes.169512: A cold front pushed across western New York triggering scattered thunderstorms over the northern Finger Lakes late in the morning. As these thunderstorms increased, a prolific amount of lightning occurred. The line then swept east across the North Country to the east of Lake Ontario into the afternoon producing straight line wind damage.
episodes.169516: Isolated strong to severe thunderstorms occurred across the southeast plains in the evening, with strong outflow winds to 65 mph the main risk on this day.
episodes.169563: A thunderstorm moving through the Detroit River produced a wind gust around 50 knots.
episodes.169585: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed across west central Arkansas during the early morning hours of the 14th. The strongest storms produced large hail to half dollar size. Isolated strong to severe thunderstorms redeveloped late in the evening across northwestern Arkansas. Moderately strong instability combined with strong deep layer wind shear promoted the development of a supercell in Washington County, which produced large hail up to ping pong ball size.||Thunderstorms that developed across northeastern Kansas during the early morning hours of the 15th, moved southeast across portions of northwestern Arkansas during the afternoon. Additional thunderstorms developed during the late afternoon and evening near the outflow boundary from these storms. The strongest storms produced large hail up to quarter size and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.169586: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed near an outflow boundary across northeastern Oklahoma during the early morning hours of the 15th. The strongest thunderstorms produced large hail up to ping pong ball size. Additional strong to severe thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and evening hours, along a southward-moving outflow boundary from earlier thunderstorms that moved through southwestern Missouri and northwestern Arkansas. The atmosphere along and south of this outflow boundary in eastern Oklahoma had become very unstable by the afternoon, and combined with strong deep layer wind shear across the area, an environment supportive of supercells was in place as the storms developed. Several supercells moved across the region, producing large hail up to softball size.
episodes.169672: An outflow boundary moving into an extremely unstable airmass sparked multiple supercell thunderstorms with very large hail close to softball sized and strong damaging wind gusts.
episodes.169684: In the upper levels a negatively tilted trough approached from the west as associated surface low pressure formed and deepened as it passed to the north and west of the CWA. A strong cold front extending down from the surface low moved through the area allowing for severe thunderstorms to develop.
episodes.169685: In the upper levels a negatively tilted trough approached from the west as associated surface low pressure formed and deepened as it passed to the north and west of the CWA. A strong cold front extending down from the surface low moved through the area allowing for severe thunderstorms to develop.
episodes.169747: A shortwave moved across Wyoming and brought severe thunderstorms with strong wind gusts. The strongest storm moved across eastern Yellowstone Park. An 82 mph wind gust was reported that blew down several trees. Heavy rain caused an avalanche that closed the East Entrance of Yellowstone Park for several hours. Other strong storms occurred in southern Wyoming where wind gusts of 66 mph were reported at the Sweetwater County Airport and 59 mph at the Big Piney Airport.
episodes.169769: A moist and unstable airmass within a warm and moist airmass spawned multiple rounds of strong to severe storms consisting of sub-severe hail and severe straight line wind gusts. The first round of storms was initiated by a weak convergence axis over the Sandhills, as well as a pre-frontal trough over the northwest Piedmont. The second round of storms was mainly focused by a trailing cold front that cleared central North Carolina by late evening.
episodes.169789: A line of severe thunderstorms moved through northeast Louisiana on the evening of May 15th. Widespread damaging winds brought down a number of trees, including several that fell onto structures and vehicles. Outflow from these thunderstorms created a dust storm across northeast Louisiana as visibilities dropped to one quarter of a mile before the rain started.
episodes.169792: A line of severe thunderstorms moved through portions of western and central Mississippi on the evening of May 15th. Widespread damaging winds downed numerous trees and power lines with several trees falling onto structures and vehicles. Outflow from these thunderstorms created a dust storm across the Mississippi Delta as visibilities dropped to one quarter of a mile before the rain started.  In addition, a separate cluster of storms in eastern Mississippi produced scattered wind damage across Noxubee County.
episodes.169797: Showers and thunderstorms along and ahead of a cold front resulted in widespread wind damage across eastern New York during the afternoon into the evening hours on May 16. There were a few severe hail reports and a funnel cloud sighting over Schoharie County.
episodes.169799: Showers and thunderstorms along and ahead of a cold front resulted in multiple damaging wind reports across northwestern Connecticut during the afternoon into the evening hours on May 16.
episodes.169800: Showers and thunderstorms along and ahead of a cold front resulted in multiple damaging wind reports across western Massachusetts during the afternoon into the evening hours on May 16.
episodes.169802: Showers and thunderstorms along and ahead of a cold front resulted in a couple of damaging wind reports across southern Vermont during the afternoon into the evening hours on May 16.
episodes.169837: An isolated severe thunderstorm produced quarter size hail and downed several trees in Adams County on the afternoon of May 16th.
episodes.169898: Convection developed during the evening hours of May 16th, associated with a shortwave moving down the back side of a departing trough.  The resulting thunderstorms created wind damage in Venango County.
episodes.169970: Isolated to widely scattered thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front during the afternoon across upstate South Carolina. A few of the storms produced large hail and brief damaging wind gusts.
episodes.169971: Isolated to widely scattered thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front during the afternoon across western North Carolina. One of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts in Polk County.
episodes.169983: A long-duration severe thunderstorm event affect Eastern NC during the afternoon, and lingered well into the evening hours. Numerous reports of wind damage occurred, along with a couple tornado reports, and some large hail.
episodes.170005: Showers and thunderstorms developed across Central and Southwest Montana, leading to strong, gusty winds, small hail, brief downpours, and an array of lightning. Dry and seasonally mild conditions returned thereafter, leading to an increase of westerly winds in excess 55 mph across the Rocky Mountain Front and adjacent plains. Cooler temperatures returned during the latter half of the week, with temperatures 10 to 20 degrees below average and widespread precipitation. Lower elevations saw generally a tenth to half an inch of liquid precipitation, whereas higher elevations saw several inches of snowfall.
episodes.170039: The region was under the influence of northwest flow in the upper levels. More importantly, the mid levels cooled and low levels warmed quite a bit compared to previous days. That combination resulted in steep lapse rates, a very unstable mid level environment. This was especially so over coastal locations of the local area, multiple storms produced severe thunderstorm winds.
episodes.170041: The region was under the influence of northwest flow in the upper levels. More importantly, the mid levels cooled and low levels warmed quite a bit compared to previous days. That combination resulted in steep lapse rates, a very unstable mid level environment. This was especially so over coastal locations of the local area, multiple storms produced very large hail.
episodes.170042: A carryover from the previous day...the region was under the influence of northwest flow in the upper levels. More importantly, the mid levels cooled and low levels warmed quite a bit compared to previous days. That combination resulted in steep lapse rates, a very unstable mid level environment. This was especially so over coastal locations of the local area, multiple storms produced severe thunderstorm winds.
episodes.170054: A cluster of storms moving out of Oklahoma moved across the northeastern quadrant of the CWA. Strong damaging winds occurred with the leading edge storms, but trailing storms produced hail. A destructive area of 95 mph winds damaged much of Honey Grove in eastern Fannin County.
episodes.170083: Scattered severe thunderstorms in advance of a cold front produced damaging winds across portions of central, eastern, and southeast Virginia.
episodes.170084: Scattered severe thunderstorms in advance of a cold front produced large hail across portions of the Lower Maryland Eastern Shore.
episodes.170094: Several weak upper level impulses provided the lift for scattered strong to severe thunderstorms to develop during the heating of the day on May 15th.  Instability parameters were higher than normal for mid May due to above normal temperatures and surface moisture.
episodes.170130: Scattered thunderstorms in advance of a cold front produced gusty winds across portions of the James River.
episodes.170131: Scattered thunderstorms in advance of a cold front produced gusty winds across portions of the Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.170132: Scattered thunderstorms in advance of a cold front produced gusty winds across portions of the Virginia Coastal Waters.
episodes.170246: Severe thunderstorms developed and produced hail in portions of coastal Alabama.
episodes.170252: Strong to severe storms produced several strong wind gusts across the Alabama and Florida nearshore waters.
episodes.170298: Low pressure moved through central New England Monday, with a warm front lifting into the region during the afternoon with showers and thunderstorms. A cold front then passed through western New Hampshire in the evening, with a line of strong to severe thunderstorms. Much of southern New Hampshire received sporadic straight line wind damage, with a video instance of a tornado between Charlestown and Claremont, NH.

A brief but damaging tornado touched down in North Charlestown, NH|Monday afternoon associated with a line of severe thunderstorms|entering western New Hampshire. EF-0 damage was observed initially|and towards termination, with around a thousand snapped and|uprooted softwood trees. The tornado strengthened north of the|Claremont, NH city line with EF-1 damage. A 90 mph microburst was determined to have hit Roach's Farm in|Venice, NY. There were four barns that sustained roof damage with|metal panels being lofted. The furthest debris was about 200 |yards from the barn. Some of the metal panels had been lofted into|the power lines along Stewart's Corners Rd but had been cleaned |prior to our survey. There were several pieces of metal roofing |that were still located in trees at the time of our survey. At the|intersection of Ford Rd and Stewart's Corners Rd, there was a |Davis weather station that was sheltered from the southwest, but |recorded a measured 59 mph gust during the storm. ||The strongest damage indicators were on the northwestern edge of |the damage path along Ford Rd, where several trees were snapped. |Three of the hemlock trees lining Ford road were snapped roughly |10 to 15 feet off the ground. Behind those trees, there were a |group of maple trees with several of those being snapped in |addition to the hemlocks. One of the maple trees fell onto a farm |building and shifted the entire building off the wooden foundation|to the east northeast. The building likely shifted due to the |tree falling, however the wooden polls on the northwestern edge of|the building had been lifted out of the ground by about 4 inches.|Other damage was also seen around the area, generally to the east|where another farm building lost metal roofing and a large |hardwood tree had its trunk snapped, however they were not along |the path of the stronger winds.
